question.text: Mr. Vikram Menon, an HNI, wants to invest in a newly launched Category II Private Equity AIF managed by Konark Capital. He is NOT an Accredited Investor, NOT an employee of the AIF, and the fund is NOT a Large Value Fund. What is the MINIMUM commitment he must make to participate?

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI (AIF) Regulations prescribe a minimum investment of INR 1 crore per investor in any AIF scheme. The relaxations — INR 25 lakh for employees/directors of the AIF, relaxed thresholds for Accredited Investors, and the Angel Fund exception of INR 10 lakh per angel investor — do not apply to Mr. Menon's profile. The Trap: INR 25 lakh is the employee carve-out; INR 50 lakh is the PMS minimum (different product); INR 10 lakh is the Angel Fund per-investor minimum and also the SIF minimum. Each is a real threshold but misapplied to a Cat II PE non-employee investor. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-A PMS Distributor exam tests the INR 50 lakh PMS minimum; XIX-A/B test the INR 1 crore AIF minimum; XIX-C expects the Manager to understand every carve-out (employee, AI, LVF, Angel) because LP onboarding depends on it. Manager's Pro-Tip: When onboarding an LP below INR 1 crore, document the exemption source in the subscription agreement's representations — 'employee of the Manager', 'Accredited Investor with current certificate dated X', or 'LVF investor' — auditors will ask for this during the annual SEBI inspection.
